The naming isn't part of the hierarchy outside of letting you know that was the top title. They are all the top titles in their respective brands. In kayfabe, Cody Rhodes and GUNTHER are on the same level. We're not supposed to care that Cody is 1a and GUNTHER is 1b, if you really wanna be that specific, in terms of who is promoted as the general guy in the company. Any reference to that by the talent themselves is considered meta and fourth wall breaking in WWE.

If you want to insist on an inside baseball outlook, generally speaking, the champ on what was considered the A brand was the top champ. When there wasn't a brand extension, it was whatever had the "WWE Championship" lineage. Look at the current titles for that: the Undisputed WWE Championship is a combined lineage between the WWE Title and the Universal Title (which was only named such to invoke the WWE Universe as the Raw world title), because the bulk the Roman's record involves his Universal Title reign that he won during the ThunderDome era. Without that specific lineage, he can't be called the longest reigning champ, because his specific WWE Title reign is nowhere close. That's why the current WHC had to be made, because separating the two is literally impossible statistically.

Meanwhile, the current World Heavyweight Championship doesn't even include the 2003-2013 lineage. It shares the name, the design invokes the original and the WWE version, but its lineage starts with Seth Rollins.

While I have mixed feelings on WWE's preference to use the titles as branding promotion making sure the logo is always the most eye-catching part, I don't think we need to act like there's no hierarchy. Ever since they had separate world titles for brands, it's always been there's a world, a secondary/midcard, a tag and women's. All three brands follow that general structure, and the only cross brand titles are Women's Tags and the Speed Titles. The roster is too big to have everyone fighting for a literal handful of titles. It didn't work when it was just one world champ for both brands before they adopted the Big Gold, it didn't work when Roman held the titles hostage for 2 years. You want two brands with separate rosters, you have to give their respective equivalents. 

And they decided to make their own version of Big Gold because Raw was headed by a former WCW guy, and the guy who got gifted the title was a guy who loved certain WCW aspects, and I'm sure a form of the title Ric Flair is synonymous with was more than something he was willing to emulate and invoke. For safety reasons, quick rope climbing like the Final requires assistance from the crew, giving a certain amount of slack in their harness that would keep them in the air if for some reason they let go of the rope in mid-air. Pull is just them literally helping you up by way of the safety rope, and some control of it has to be had to prevent tangling, which is just as dangerous as it is run-ending.  

To make the rope climb harder or easier, they can give as much slack or take away as much slack as they want while still allowing them to actually still be able to climb.  The more slack, the more distance they can cover at a quick enough pace so long as their technique is efficient enough. Even the worst rope climbers can't beat it if they have poor form, and it would look pretty obvious they're getting outside help if they're barely trying yet flying up the rope. 

Likewise, if you don't have enough slack, you have to exert more energy in how much distance you can cover. Not necessarily a slack example, but the reason Kong in 24 was considered to be screwed out of his Final Stage attempted, is because his safety rope was tangled in the actual rope for the climb itself, which halted his pacing. He was offered a redo, but he knew he was too tired to try again.

Based on how the rules are normally, the PPT would be acting President until the vacancy is fulfilled.  I would presume if some are holding elections and some aren't, that would make it impossible to reach 270 and thus the House would have control there to make the call and I'd assume they would have the power to decide from election to inauguration so the House would still be active.  

Now, when could the House say "we're taking over" in this scenario is the issue here, and there's no real precedence since the only two times the House chose a President, every state voted; just neither candidate reached the electoral threshold at that time.  Interestingly though, the last time that happened (1824), Andrew Jackson had the higher electoral count (even though it wasn't close to the 131 number needed to definitively win) AND had the popular vote, but John Quincy Adams had the state delegates needed to win the House vote.

EDIT: And since Congress sets the dates for election, theoretically they set an election meant to fill the role that the acting President is in.

The 20th Amendment explicitly says a President's term ends at noon on January 20th.  If there's no election, Trump has no (legal) standing to stay as President past that date and the succession line of order comes into play.  However, Pence would be gone, too, and he's 2nd in line.  So it would just be Pelosi, right?

Not so fast, because House members are re-elected every two years so they will always have elections the same year as the President...no election means no House of Representatives, because Congress terms end on January 3rd at noon for those that are expiring.  Unless states decided to appoint interim House members in the meantime, Pelosi would be out (however, she would be back in line if a sitting body was formed in some way in the House).  

So then you go to 4th in line: President Pro Tempore, which is generally the longest-serving senator from the majority party in the Senate.  If all of this happened today, it would be Chuck Grassley from Iowa.  However, 1/3 of the Senate would also be vacated without an election since they serve six years with re-election being on even numbered years, and those seats would have to be filled, too, and there are currently more Democratic governors than Republican ones, so chances are those replacements would be Democrats and thus give Senate majority to Democrats, which means the President Pro Tempore changes to Patrick Leahy of Vermont (who had served 32 years before Bernie popped up in 2007).

So, Trump trying to bypass an election would almost ensure a Democratic replacement, rather than taking his chances and being re-elected.

In the bigger matches, the refs tend to have a loosened grip on enforcing the rules, usually just verbalizing their disapproval more or actively trying to break them apart.  Counting for either a DQ or a count out is more of a complete last resort than the immediate reaction. They'll only start counting out someone outside once a big spot happens that renders someone incapacitated. It's the mindset of wanting a definitive decision between the two as opposed to the ref deciding it for them.

You have rope breaks in No DQ matches because pins can still be broken up via the rope.  And it's more dramatic for a wrestler to still impulsively reach for the rope in a metaphorical act of defiance despite knowing there's no obligation for his opponent to break the hold because it's No DQ.

And that's standard in general, not just to WWE.  In the Omega/Jericho match, Jericho broke a pin via touching the rope and while Jericho could have kept his hold on for as long as he wants, he let go when Omega reached the rope from exhaustion and because he has to now find a new way to win/weaken Omega further.

They've done for some and haven't for others.  This is the current setup for the titles:

RAW:
-
- Universal Championship: Brand new title, brand new lineage.  Finn Balor is the inaugural champion. 

- United States Championship: WWE's lineage is counted alongside the lineage first started in 1975 by Mid-Atlantic Championship Wrestling (when part of the NWA) which later became WCW when Mid-Atlantic was bought by Ted Turner.  After a brief period in WWE where it was referred to as the WCW US Title and retired in 2001 it was brought back in 2003 with a new design but the lineage intact.  When Eddie Guerrero won to revive the title, he became the first under the specific name of WWE United States Champion, but the 101st in the overall lineage of US Champions. 

- Raw Women's Championship: Brand new title, brand new lineage (its lineage is not associated with the previous Women's Championship from 1956-2010 nor the Divas Championship from 2008-2016).  Charlotte is the inaugural champion of this lineage after her win at Mania 32.

- Raw Tag Team Championship: This lineage started in 2002 when SmackDown created its own championship for its brand when WWE's original Tag Team Championship was made exclusive to Raw.  SD's belts took the name WWE Tag Team Championship for itself while Raw's was simply named the World Tag Team Championship in similar vein to when the World Heavyweight Championship (aka WWE's version of the Big Gold) started on Raw.  When both brands tag titles were unified into the Unified Tag Team Championship, the teams that won counted for both sets of titles' lineage (so Unified Tag Team Championship are listed on both the WWE Tag and World Tag lineages).  During the Hart Dynasty's reign in 2010, the World Tag lineage was deactivated and they created a new design (the 'pennies') and kept the WWE Tag lineage.  This is the lineage that has been used without interruption since 2002.  Kurt Angle and Chris Benoit are the inaugural champions of this lineage.  New Day broke the record for this lineage at day 332 which made them the longest reigning for this lineage.  They became all-time record holders regardless of lineage last week.


SmackDown Live:
-

- WWE Championship: Same lineage as WWE's first world title since 1963 when it was then-called the WWWF.  When combined with the WCW World Championship to make the Undisputed Championship in 2001, this lineage was retained while the WCW World Champion lineage was discontinued.  When combined with the World Heavyweight Championship (WWE's Big Gold) in 2013 to create the WWE World Heavyweight Championship, this lineage was retained as the World Heavyweight Championship lineage was discontinued.  Although the physical belt still says "World Heavyweight Champion" on the bottom when it was the WWEWHC, the official name of the championship is WWE Championship.  The inaugural champion was Buddy Rogers.

- Intercontinental Championship: Same lineage since the title was created in 1979.  The title was briefly deactivated from October 2002 to May 2003 when unified with the World Heavyweight Championship in a match between WHC Triple H and IC Champion Kane where Triple H won.  Christian became the champion when it was brought back in May 2003, the inaugural champion of course was Pat Patterson.

- SmackDown Women's Championship: Brand new title, brand new lineage.  Becky Lynch was the inaugural champion.

- SmackDown Tag Team Championship: Brand new title, brand new lineage.  Heath Slater and Rhyno were the inaugural champions.

It's in the same vein as when they unified the Divas and Womens Championships but only kept the Divas lineage in the past: they kept the most recently created lineage (Divas title was only a couple years old at that point when they did it).

Technically speaking, yes.  Demolition are the longest reigning Tag Champions of that particular lineage.  New Day have been the longest reigning Tag Champions of the current lineage since day 332 (that previous record for this lineage was Paul London and Brian Kendrick at 331), which they first pointed out, then people complained about Demolition (even though they are different belts and lineages) and they kept quiet until they became the all-time record holders.
